page: Microsoft Azure E96s_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Esv7 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 96 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 48 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes an L3 cache of 480 MB, alongside 2 MB of L2 cache and 48 KB of L1d cache. The system is equipped with 768.0 GB of RAM, yielding a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable for remote storage attachments.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong multi-core and memory performance. The server achieved a top-tier PassMark CPU score of 109,110.34 and a multi-core stress-ng CPU performance of 102,250.79. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with cached small-block read-only operations reaching 7,543.56 GB/sec, placing it in the top tier, while uncached large-block reads and writes reached 349.82 GB/sec and 134.51 GB/sec respectively. The processor's advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 and AMX, contribute to top-tier performance in CPU encryption and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Database operations are also robust, with Redis SET operations reaching 160.72 million operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E96s_v7 provides high resource density for memory-intensive workloads without the added cost of local NVMe drives or dedicated GPUs. It is optimized for enterprise databases, large-scale in-memory analytics, Redis caching layers, and heavy web serving, where its static web serving throughput of 151.85 GB/sec is highly advantageous. Additionally, the presence of Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions enables efficient CPU-based LLM inference, particularly for prompt processing where it achieves top-tier token throughput across small, medium, and large models.
